user_input:
The concept of "reality" is complex and subjective, and different people may have different definitions of what is real. In general, reality refers to the objective, independent, and physical world that exists independently of our perception or consciousness.
As for how we know something is real, there are a few different ways that we can determine the reality of a given experience or perception. One way is through our senses: we can use our senses of sight, touch, hearing, taste, and smell to perceive the world around us, and we can trust that these sensory experiences are giving us a relatively accurate representation of reality.
Another way we can determine the reality of something is through scientific investigation. Scientific methods, such as observation, experimentation, and analysis, can help us to understand and verify the nature of reality. Scientific findings are based on empirical evidence and are subject to testing and verification, which adds to their credibility.
Ultimately, whether or not something is real is a matter of ongoing debate and investigation, and it is likely that our understanding of reality will continue to evolve and change as we continue to learn more about the world around us.
